raw_comment:
I noticed that most of the country is experiencing some sort of drought, and despite being next to a coast or a mountain range, lots of places are facing increasingly severe droughts.

I wonder why: Why is it that these places, that have a lot of access to oceans, lakes, rivers, and mountains are facing so much lack of freshwater? How is this happening, and what can we do to fix it?

Water relates to me and my community by affecting our climate and environment first. Forest fires, for example, ravage our communities, displacing many people who often, have not much more than what they've lost.

A good headline is:
America's Water: Drought Killing Communities one-by-one
